summary: Audited the Pointer, Tensor, Layout, and core layout-construction/view APIs. Added terse traced-execution contracts and examples, replaced display-like examples with executable assertions, and corrected the misleading implication that layout((1, 2)) is a two-mode coordinate: the supported spelling is layout(1, 2), and scalar IntTuple results require get_scalar. A regression covers both the rejected nested profile and the supported mapping/inverse.

tests.what_was_measured: All layout algebra tests passed after the documentation regression was added (32 passed, 1 skipped); raw output: /job/raw-output/layout-algebra-final.txt

Verified required docstrings, the documented static shape/stride, coordinate-to-index result 9, inverse coordinate (1, 2), and rejection of the extra-nested layout((1, 2)) form; raw output: /job/raw-output/docstring-layout-example-final.txt

Ran raw Pointer load/store and element-offset behavior on one AMD Instinct MI355X and compared output numerically with PyTorch addition (max-error assertion below 1e-5); raw output: /job/raw-output/pointer-gpu.txt

Ran Tensor shape, indexing, fragment load/store, and layout operations on one AMD Instinct MI355X; the example printed PASS after torch.allclose(A + B, C); raw output: /job/raw-output/tensor-vector-add.txt
Formatting/lint command could not run because ruff is not installed in the prepared interpreter; raw output: /job/raw-output/ruff.txt

remaining_limitations: No C++ or native compiler source changed, so the prepared native rebuild was not applicable. The reviewed task was limited to Pointer/Tensor/layout APIs; the broader upstream request to document every public symbol under expr/compiler/utils remains outside this PR. Direct upstream issue API inspection was blocked by the authenticated token lifetime policy, so the supplied upstream snapshot and accessible mirror issue were used. Ruff was unavailable in the prepared interpreter.
